profile.name: Michael Bridgford
profile.bio: Michael Bridgford is an independent candidate for Iowa's 1st district who grew up on a seventh-generation family farm. He describes himself as a small-business owner, and Wikipedia lists him as an independent financial advisor.

platform.point: Supports term limits, a congressional stock-trading ban and campaign finance reform.
Wants healthcare price transparency and revived rural clinics.
Seeks to fix Social Security before it reaches a funding crisis.
Calls for strict oversight of AI data centers and technology companies.
Supports farmers, the biofuels industry, small businesses and manufacturing revival.

economy.evidence: Pairs fiscal responsibility with healthcare price transparency and strict guardrails on Big Tech.

tech.evidence: Calls for strict guardrails on AI data centers and Big Tech.

profile.name: Rick Stewart
profile.bio: Rick Stewart has run for office in Iowa several times: as an independent for U.S. Senate in 2014, for Iowa Secretary of Agriculture in 2018, as the Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate in 2020, and as the Libertarian nominee for governor in 2022, when he received about 2.4 percent of the vote.
profile.notes: Wikipedia lists him only as having filed paperwork for the Libertarian nomination, and a June 2026 state objections panel removed two Libertarian candidates from the ballot, so his ballot status should be checked. No 2026 campaign site or platform was found.

profile.name: Dave Bushaw
profile.bio: Dave Bushaw is from northeast Iowa, raised in West Union and living in Hawkeye, and started a small squash farm at 19. He spent about five years as a Midwest organizer for the rural group United Today, Stronger Tomorrow, organized for Bernie Sanders' 2020 campaign, and performs as a folk and labor musician. The Forward Party has endorsed him.

platform.point: Wants to improve economic conditions so young people are not pushed to leave Iowa.
Highlights stronger workers' rights and organized labor conditions.
Focuses on improving health care access in rural communities.
Pitches an independent, working-class voice focused on accountability and transparency in Washington.

profile.notes: Stated priorities were too general to score; his site's platform page was not reviewed in detail.

profile.name: Brendan Gomez
profile.bio: Brendan Gomez is the Constitution Party nominee for Idaho's 1st congressional district. He was also the party's nominee for the seat in 2024.
profile.notes: No campaign website or public policy statements were found; Ballotpedia could not be retrieved.

profile.name: Will Johanson
profile.bio: Will Johanson is an engineer in Idaho's semiconductor industry and a U.S. Navy veteran who served as a nuclear machinist's mate aboard the USS Georgia until 2020. He holds bachelor's and master's degrees in materials science and engineering from Boise State University. He was raised in California's Central Valley and is based in Boise.

platform.point: Argues government overreach and red tape hurt working families and slow innovation.
Prioritizes fiscal responsibility and reducing the national debt.
Supports a strong national defense.
Highlights energy and gas prices as a campaign focus.
Pledges to defend constitutional rights and individual liberties.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on limited government, fiscal responsibility and cutting bureaucratic red tape.

profile.notes: Campaign site lists broad themes without detailed policy proposals.

profile.name: Carta Sierra
profile.bio: Carta Sierra is the Constitution Party nominee for Idaho's 2nd congressional district. Sierra was also the party's nominee for the seat in 2024.
profile.notes: No campaign website or public policy statements were found; Ballotpedia could not be retrieved.

profile.name: Emre Houser
profile.current_role: Small-business owner and Idaho National Guard member
profile.bio: Emre Houser is an Idaho small-business owner of more than 15 years with over 27 years of military service. He served in the Air Force from 1995 to 1999, including at Mountain Home Air Force Base, and has served in the Idaho National Guard since 1999, deploying to Iraq in 2003. He has lived in Idaho for nearly 30 years.

platform.point: Pledges to defend constitutional principles and answer only to Idaho voters.
Aims to protect Idaho's public lands.
Campaigns against the influence of billionaires in politics.
Wants to move past culture wars and refocus government on helping citizens.

profile.notes: Social handles are listed on the campaign site as @houserforidaho; exact profile URLs were not individually verified.

profile.name: Tripp Hutchinson
profile.bio: Tripp Hutchinson is a member of the Ketchum City Council. He was born and raised in Idaho and is running as an independent for Idaho's 2nd congressional district.

platform.point: Wants Idaho families to be able to live comfortably on a single household income.
Supports independent local businesses.
Aims to preserve Idaho's rural land.
Opposes consolidation of corporate and government power and advocates citizen self-determination.
Refuses money from billionaires and corporate PACs.

profile.notes: Campaign themes are broad and do not support scoring specific policy domains.
